title: Factors Associated With Positive Post-Treatment STI Tests and Sexual Knowledge, Attitudes, Behaviors and Practices
official: Factors Associated With a Positive Post-Treatment Test for Sexually Transmitted Infections Caused by Chlamydia Trachomatis and/or Neisseria Gonorrhoeae in Relation to Sexual Knowledge, Attitudes, Behaviors and Practices (KABP): A Prospective Longitudinal Single-Center Study
summary:
The goal of this study is to understand why some adults continue to test positive for chlamydia or gonorrhea after receiving antibiotic treatment.

The study will also explore whether sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices are linked to positive test results after treatment.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

How many participants test positive for chlamydia or gonorrhea four or eight weeks after treatment? Are differences in sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices linked to positive test results? Are treatment adherence and sexual behaviors after treatment linked to positive test results? The study will include 238 adults diagnosed with chlamydia, gonorrhea, or both infections at the Centre Hospitalier de Martigues in France.

Participants will:

Receive standard antibiotic treatment as part of their usual medical care. Answer a questionnaire about their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices.

Attend two follow-up visits, approximately four and eight weeks after their initial visit.

Provide samples for additional laboratory tests to check for chlamydia or gonorrhea at both follow-up visits.

Answer questions about their treatment and sexual behaviors during follow-up. The researchers will compare participants who test positive after treatment with those who test negative. This comparison may help identify factors linked to persistent infection or a new infection.

Participation is voluntary. The study does not involve experimental medication or changes to the usual antibiotic treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Adults aged 18 years or older, regardless of sex.

Confirmed Chlamydia trachomatis and/or Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection diagnosed by nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT/PCR) or culture at the Centre Hospitalier de Martigues.

Symptomatic or asymptomatic individuals receiving medical care for a sexually transmitted infection.

No antibiotic treatment targeting Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae within the 7 days preceding enrollment.

Individuals who have received written and oral information about the study and have provided free, informed, written consent after an appropriate reflection period.

Individuals agreeing to attend the scheduled follow-up visits.

Individuals able to read, understand, and complete the study questionnaires in French, including the KABP questionnaire.

Individuals accepting the specific research procedures in accordance with applicable regulations.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Individuals younger than 18 years.

Absence of microbiological confirmation of Chlamydia trachomatis and/or Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection by NAAT/PCR or culture.

Antibiotic treatment targeting Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae initiated before enrollment.

Individuals deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision.

Individuals under legal protection measures (guardianship, curatorship, or judicial protection) or otherwise unable to provide informed consent, in accordance with the study protocol.

Individuals who do not sufficiently understand French to receive study information or complete the questionnaires.

Individuals unable to comply with the scheduled follow-up visits or study-specific procedures.

Individuals who refuse to participate or decline to sign the informed consent form.

Individuals participating in another interventional study that may interfere with the objectives of ECART-IST.

Individuals whose medical condition or situation, as assessed by the investigator, makes optimal participation impossible or may compromise the quality of the collected data.
